- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use sentiment-weighted moving average.
- When sentiment is volatile or erratic (alternating 0.3–0.8), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use 3-day smoothing to reduce noise.
- In low-sentiment periods, model underestimates true price; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to account for suppressed demand or policy-driven support.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use sentiment as a volatility proxy: if sentiment <0.4, reduce forecast variance by 10–20% to reflect subdued market reaction.
